Abstract 
Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is a classic optimization algorithm; however, it 
has issues when solving high-dimensional complex optimization problems, such 
as sensitivity to initial parameters, insufficient population diversity, and susceptibility 
to becoming stuck in local optima. To this end, we propose a particle swarm 
optimization algorithm with multiple swarm strategies (GPSOM) that significantly 
improves the algorithm’s optimization performance by designing grouping 
and diversification strategies for the population. GPSOM divides the population 
into three subgroups and adopts targeted strategies based on different phases: sub-
swarm 1 focuses on exploration and improves population diversity and local search 
ability by dynamically adjusting operators; sub-swarm 2 focuses on exploitation, 
introducing sine cosine factors and adaptive mechanisms to traverse the solution 
space efficiently; sub-swarm 3 achieves global and local balance, generating high-
quality solutions through adaptive factors and position adjustment operators. The 
experimental results show that GPSOM performs significantly better than traditional 
algorithms on the Combinatorial Evolutionary Computing (CEC) 2020 benchmark 
test set (hereinafter referred to as 20TS), and its reliability and efficiency have been 
demonstrated in practical applications, such as 15 engineering examples, vehicle 
cruise control, and robot path optimization. GPSOM is an efficient, stable, practical 
optimization algorithm that effectively solves high-dimensional complex optimization 
problems.

and accelerating industrial technology development. Therefore, studying optimization 
problems has significant theoretical significance and considerable practical impact.

Although the CI field has made remarkable progress, it still faces some specific

rely on empirical data and expert knowledge, which may be challenging to obtain 
in some complex and dynamically changing systems [3]. Second, NN have robust

However, the performance of these algorithms is often affected by factors such as the

In the face of the above challenges and problems, this study aims to develop a new 
nature-inspired optimization algorithm that combines the strengths of SI and EC to 
exhibit higher efficiency and robustness in solving real-world optimization problems. 
Therefore, a new multi-group strategy particle swarm optimization algorithm was 
proposed. The global search ability and local exploitation accuracy of the algorithm 
are improved effectively through the fine division of the population and the custom 
strategy, and the adaptability and robustness of the algorithm are enhanced. The main 
contributions and innovations of this study are summarized as follows:
1.	 To overcome the drawbacks of slow convergence speed, sensitivity to initial 
parameters, susceptibility to local optima, and uneven distribution of solution 
space in PSO, a single population is divided into three subgroups with different 
update strategies (exploration, exploitation, equilibrium) in GPSOM, and 
corresponding strategies are implemented for each subgroup. During the search 
phase, operator A was adjusted to enhance the algorithm’s ability to search for new 
solution space regions and to avoid premature convergence. In the exploitation 
phase, sine cosine factors and a self-protection mechanism of Genghis Khan 
shark optimizer (GKSO) [6] were added to improve the algorithm’s local search 
capability of the algorithm. In the equilibrium phase, a weight factor Coef  is set, 
and the search strategy is dynamically adjusted to maintain population diversity 
while effectively improving the quality of the solution.
2.	 Qualitative and population diversity analyses were conducted using the GPSOM 
algorithm on the 20TS. To verify the effectiveness of various strategies in the 
GPSOM algorithm, ablation experiments were conducted on the 20TS in 10D. At 
the same time, comparative experiments were conducted on GPSOM with partially 
improved PSO, newly proposed algorithms, and other improved algorithms in the 50 
and 100D of this test set to evaluate and analyze the performance of GPSOM.
3.	 GPSOM was applied to the path optimization of 15 engineering examples, a 
vehicle cruise control system, and a mobile robot. This prove that GPSOM is highly 
applicable to solving practical problems.

Classification of improved PSO
Scholars have proposed various improved PSO methods to address its inherent 
limitations and adapt to different optimization problems. This study collected some PSO 
improvement algorithms and divided them into three categories: parameter adjustment, 
multi-strategy improvement, and grouping-based PSO. Table 1 lists the algorithms used 
for PSO improvement in recent years.
PSO for parameter adjustment
Parameter adjustment is an important means of improving the performance of PSO 
algorithm and can usually be divided into the following four types: inertia weight 
adjustment, chaotic search strategy, adaptive adjustment, and contraction factor 
adjustment. The improved chaotic PSO (ICPSO) [8] modifies the inertia term of 
traditional PSO through chaotic mapping, aiming to maximize the power generation of 
photovoltaic arrays in different environmental backgrounds. However, chaotic mapping 
is sensitive to initial values, which may decrease algorithm stability, particularly in 
complex multimodal problems where its performance is limited. Linear Decreasing 
Inertial Weight Particle Swarm Optimization for Global Optimization (LDIW-PSO) [9] 
integrates a linearly decreasing inertia weight (LDIW) mechanism to improve the global 
search capability of traditional PSO technology. Although its global search capability 
has been enhanced, linearly decreasing inertia weights may lead to insufficient local 
search capability in some cases, thereby affecting the acquisition of accurate solutions. 
Supervised weight learning-based PSO (XSummPSO) [10] extracts relevant information 
from automated text by optimizing the weights assigned to each feature. This method 
performs well in text extraction tasks, but its effectiveness in processing structured or 
semi-structured data requires further validation. Constriction Factor PSO (CFPSO) [11] 
introduces constraint factors to improve system stability and convergence, enhancing

Improved PSO with multiple strategies
The PSO performance can be significantly improved by combining different particle 
update rules, global and local optimal solution selection methods, and other algorithmic 
strategies. A quantum PSO algorithm with the elite opposition-based learning strategy 
(EOL-QPSO) [14] introduced Elite Opponent Learning (EOL) to further optimize 
the performance of the Quantum Potential Model (QPSO) for particle swarm spatial 
position updates. However, EOL requires many computing resources, and may not be 
suitable for applications with high real-time requirements. A hybrid PSO with marine 
predators (HMPPSO) [15] is an algorithm for solving the behavioural problems of 
marine predators, utilizing a multi-stage search strategy to balance exploration and 
exploitation. Although this method performs well in dynamic search environments, 
its complex search mechanism may increase algorithm time complexity. The Multi-
strategy Learning-based PSO Algorithm (IPSosono) [16] is an internal multi rate PSO 
method applied to the threshold image segmentation technology in enhanced COVID-
19 medical imaging. However, its universality and adaptability to other fields require 
further research and verification. A novel hybrid PSO using adaptive strategy (ASPSO) 
[17] combines chaotic mapping, elite and dimension learning strategies, adaptive 
position update strategies, and competitive substitution mechanisms to significantly 
improve the population diversity of the algorithm and avoid falling into local optima. 
However, the parameter settings of this method are relatively complex and may limit its 
practical application.
PSO with multiple populations
The risk of the algorithm becoming stuck in local optima can be effectively reduced 
by dividing the particle swarm into different subgroups and conducting independent 
parallel searches within each group. However, the rationality of the grouping mechanism 
is crucial to the algorithm’s performance.
Multiple adaptive co-evolved PSO (ACEPSO) [18] combines adaptive population 
grouping methods, the advantages and disadvantages of co-evolution mechanisms, 
and co-evolution mechanisms and adaptive mutation strategies. This demonstrates the 
significant benefits of solving diverse and complex optimization problems. However, 
excessive strategy stacking may make it challenging to optimize the algorithm and reduce 
practical application efficiency. Multiple populations co-evolutionary PSO (MPCoPSO) 
[19] effectively solves the multi-objective optimization challenge in the MoCCPOP 
model using various sets of co evolutionary PSO. However, the process of co-evolution

its adaptability to other complex optimization problems still requires further proof. In 
addition, the algorithm’s dependence on directional angles may lead to performance

GPSOM

Abstract: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is a classic optimization algorithm; however, it has issues when solving high-dimensional complex optimization problems, such as sensitivity to initial parameters, insufficient population diversity, and susceptibility to becoming stuck in local optima. To this end, we propose a particle swarm optimization algorithm with multiple swarm strategies (GPSOM) that significantly improves the algorithm’s optimization performance by designing grouping and diversification strategies for the population. GPSOM divides the population into three subgroups and adopts targeted strategies based on different phases: sub- swarm 1 focuses on exploration and improves population diversity and local search ability by dynamically adjusting operators; sub-swarm 2 focuses on exploitation, introducing sine cosine factors and adaptive mechanisms to traverse the solution space efficiently; sub-swarm 3 achieves global and local balance, generating high- quality solutions through adaptive factors and position adjustment operators. The experimental results show that GPSOM performs significantly better than traditional algorithms on the Combinatorial Evolutionary Computing (CEC) 2020 benchmark test set (hereinafter referred to as 20TS), and its reliability and efficiency have been demonstrated in practical applications, such as 15 engineering examples, vehicle cruise control, and robot path optimization. GPSOM is an efficient, stable, practical optimization algorithm that effectively solves high-dimensional complex optimization problems.
